BUDGET MANAGEMENT
In fiscal 2026, the World Bank Group evolved its budget
processes to enhance transparency and efficiency.
These reforms established a more integrated budget
framework across IFC, MIGA, and the World Bank,
linking business planning, workforce planning,
and budget decisions more directly to institutional
priorities and development outcomes. They simplified
planning and reporting processes, improved visibility
of total resources, and introduced stronger tools for
management oversight. The reforms also streamlined
cost-sharing arrangements, improved the treatment
of donor and external funding, reduced some clientfacing fees, and strengthened financial forecasting
and revenue visibility. They further supported financial
sustainability by creating efficiencies and redeploying
resources to fund strategic priorities.

We have fully embraced AI tools at the World Bank
Group, and we support clients to adopt, adapt, and
then advance them for their own needs. Our client
engagements focus on Small AI — affordable, fitfor-purpose solutions designed for local conditions,
including places with limited power, connectivity,
and computing capacity. This is not a second-best
path. It is a practical way to strengthen workers,
help firms grow, improve services, support local
entrepreneurs, and create more and better jobs.
There is much more to do, and no institution
can meet the jobs challenge alone. But this
year demonstrated what is possible when our
shareholders, clients, partners, and staff work
together with urgency and purpose.
The World Bank Group is faster, simpler, and
better equipped to deliver. Now we must build
on that progress — and help create more jobs for
more people.
